title: 不，Dario Amodei，我们不会在 5 到 10 年内治愈癌症和“大多数人类疾病”
author: Gary Marcus
content:
On Saturday, Dario Amodei claimed (in a long defense of his company’s approach to AI) that he thinks it “will actually be possible to cure most human disease in ~5-10 years”, highlighting “curing cancer” among other goals. As usual, some in the media ate it up.

And I wish it were true. But his timeline is so naive as to be absurd, both with respect to how medical science works and why it is challenging.

If you haven’t already done so, I strongly recommend you read (or reread) the March essay I wrote about AI and cancer, which builds on an essay by Emilia Javorsky. That essay started with Javorsky’s observation that (as of March) not one drug designed by AI had yet reached clinical adoption, even after over a decade of efforts.

Part of the crux of my essay (and hers) was that even if AI were a lot better, curing disease is hard, both economically and technically, and you also can’t simply skip the time-consuming clinical work. (I further argued that we don’t really have the right kind of causally- and biologically-sophisticated AI yet. New advances in AI and math don’t fundamentally change what I wrote there.)

The happy news is that you don’t have to take my word for any of this anymore. The mood has changed, and this time a whole pile of people pushed back. I have yet to see Amodei’s ridiculous claim dissected in the mainstream media, but below are some of the many tweets over the weekend that rightly took Amodei to task.

Let’s start with Eric Topol, a well-respected and very pro-AI physician/researcher who is having none of it. (Topol also notes that Hassabis made a similar absurd argument last year on 60 Minutes, maybe the most naive things I have ever heard Hassabis say. AI might someday contribute as Hassabis says, but certainly not in the next decade. Many of the quotes below happened to be directed to Amodei, who was in the news, but apply to what Hassabis claimed as well.)

Eric Topol@EricTopol
I'm keen on AI having a transformational impact on human health. But these cure projections are wildly off-base and impossible.

Lior Pachter@lpachter
We don’t even know what all the human diseases are.

Computational biologist Keith Robison:

Keith Robison@OmicsOmicsBlog
Sorry, but anyone claiming AI is curing most diseases in 5-10 years is spewing magical thinking & it’s very cruel for patients to be misled this way No matter how clever your AI is, proving we can trust it is clever takes preclinical & clinical work, which eats that timeline
Dario Amodei @DarioAmodei
2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI.  I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative.  In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I

Cancer biologist John Herrman wrote (plausibly if optimistically, but nowhere near as optimistically as Amodei):

John Herrmann, PhD@ablT315I
@EricTopol @GaryMarcus Much more defensible: AI could plausibly accelerate a few medical breakthroughs over next 10 years that surpass today’s best advances. That’s far different from “AI will cure most human disease” including complex dynamically evolving disease states like many malignancies etc

2 Likes

MD/PhD Marios Georgakis asks:

(As far as I know, the correct answer to the question about real plans posed in the first sentence is a simple “no”.)

The software engineer/enterpreneur Chombe Bupe, responding to Georgakis, adds:

Chomba Bupe@ChombaBupe
The lack of causal understanding in today's artificial intelligence (AI) systems means the models would generate a ton of proposals for potential cures for diseases most of which would be wrong & it would take a lot of effort to wade through all of that slop, I mean proposals.
Marios Georgakis @MariosGeorgakis
Has any of the AI companies ever presented a real plan for how they are going to cure even one disease in 5-10 years? This doesn't just sound crazy to ordinary people, but also to any clinician or drug developer I know. Beyond the fact that we still have very few true cures for

Even the ultimate AI optimist, Wharton professor Ethan Mollick, wasn’t really buying:

Ethan Mollick@emollick
I, also, would like more precision around discussions of how AI will cure diseases. I assume it means "a nation of geniuses in a data center will invent things that should in theory cure diseases" but there is a real big gap between that and actual trials & proof & FDA approval.

Has any of the AI companies ever presented a real plan for how they are going to cure even one disease in 5-10 years? This doesn't just sound crazy to ordinary people, but also to any clinician or drug developer I know. Beyond the fact that we still have very few true cures for

Penultimate words to Dr. Catharine Young, a Senior Fellow at the Harvard Chan School of Public Health, in a brutal pair of tweets further underscoring Amodei’s naïveté with respect to medicine.

Dr. Catharine Young@DrCatharineY
PSA: Cancer is not one disease. It is more than 200 distinct diseases, all with different causes, biology and mechanisms. Scientists who study cancer rarely talk about “curing cancer” because it’s nothing more than an empty slogan.
Polymarket Money @PolymarketMoney
BREAKING: Anthropic’s CEO declares AI companies can win back public trust by “actually curing cancer.”
2:24 AM · Aug 17, 2026 · 3.7K Views
10 Replies · 18 Reposts · 87 Likes

and

Dr. Catharine Young@DrCatharineY
Somebody needs to do an internship at the FDA.
Polymarket @Polymarket
JUST IN: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts AI could make it possible to “cure most human disease” within 5-10 years.
10:28 PM · Aug 16, 2026 · 9.05K Views
19 Replies · 15 Reposts · 178 Likes

§

There are a great many things about Amodei that I respect, including both his technical chops and business sense, as well as his bravery in standing up to the US government on important matters. But his habit of giving people unrealistic hope is not one of them. (See also the time he claimed that AI could double human lifespan by the end of the decade.)

In fairness, Amodei may believe what he says, but in that case he ought take Dr. Young’s suggestion of doing a medical internship, in order to better calibrate his understanding of the challenges in medicine.

aiSummary: 这篇文章批评了 Dario Amodei 关于 AI 将在 5-10 年内治愈大多数人类疾病的说法，认为医学复杂性、临床试验要求和当前 AI 的局限性使这样的时间表不切实际。
oneSentenceSummary: 这篇文章批评了 Dario Amodei 关于 AI 将在 5-10 年内治愈大多数人类疾病的说法，认为医学复杂性、临床试验要求和当前 AI 的局限性使这样的时间表不切实际。
summary: Gary Marcus 对 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 的乐观预测提出质疑，该预测认为 AI 能在大约 5 到 10 年内治愈包括癌症在内的大多数人类疾病。他指出，即使 AI 能生成有前景的候选药物，漫长且不确定的临床前和临床测试过程也无法被绕开，且成功率仍然很低。Marcus 强调，当前的 AI 系统缺乏深层的因果和生物学理解，常常产生大量需要广泛筛选的虚假线索。Lior Pachter 等专家指出，我们仍不清楚人类疾病的完整目录，仅癌症就包含 200 多种不同的疾病实体，这使得笼统的治愈说法毫无意义。历史证据表明，经过十多年的努力，还没有任何 AI 设计的药物进入临床采用，凸显了炒作与现实之间的差距。文章汇总了 Eric Topol、Keith Robison 和 Catharine Young 博士等受人尊敬人物的批评反应，得出结论：虽然 AI 最终可能为医学做出贡献，但目前的时间表既天真又可能具有误导性。

mainPoints.point: 疾病治愈需要漫长的临床验证，这无法通过 AI 预测来绕过。
mainPoints.explanation: 即使 AI 生成了有前景的候选药物，临床前和临床测试也需要多年时间，且成功率很低，这使得快速治愈的时间表不切实际。

mainPoints.point: 当前的 AI 系统缺乏深层的因果和生物学理解，会产生许多需要广泛筛选的假阳性结果。
mainPoints.explanation: 缺乏机制性洞察时，AI 生成的假设往往不正确，浪费资源并可能误导患者。

mainPoints.point: 专家指出，我们仍不清楚人类疾病的完整目录，仅癌症就包含 200 多种不同的疾病实体，这使得笼统的治愈说法毫无意义。
mainPoints.explanation: 疾病的异质性削弱了在单一时间表内治愈“大多数”疾病的想法。

mainPoints.point: 尽管对 AI 持乐观态度，但经过十多年的努力，还没有任何 AI 设计的药物进入临床采用，这表明承诺与现实之间存在差距。
mainPoints.explanation: 历史证据显示转化成功有限，促使人们对近期的突破性声明保持谨慎。

keyQuotes: 我希望这是真的。但他的时间表如此天真，以至于荒谬，无论从医学科学的运作方式还是其挑战性来看都是如此。
我们甚至不知道人类疾病都有哪些。
抱歉，但任何声称 AI 在 5-10 年内治愈大多数疾病的人都是在散布魔法思维，以这种方式误导患者非常残忍。
癌症不是一种疾病。它是 200 多种不同的疾病，各有不同的病因、生物学和机制。
有哪家 AI 公司提出过真正的计划，说明他们将如何在 5-10 年内治愈哪怕一种疾病吗？
